name: monday_reversal_5s
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: Indian markets exhibit a 'Monday effect' where stocks that declined on Friday tend to recover on Monday morning, and stocks that rallied on Friday tend to give back gains. This is driven by retail trader behavior: retail sells before weekends (risk aversion) creating artificial selling pressure on Friday, which reverses on Monday when institutional flow resumes. Edge persists because the effect is small and requires systematic execution to exploit — not worth it for manual traders.
mechanism: The opening auction concentrates overnight information into a single price discovery event. The first 3-5 minutes see elevated order flow as overnight orders execute. After this initial burst, predictable patterns emerge as institutional algorithms begin their daily TWAP/VWAP schedules, creating directional pressure for 15-30 minutes.

exit.signal_exit: close crosses VWAP against trade direction

weaknesses: Only trades on Mondays — 52 potential trading days per year maximum
Monday effect has been weakening globally as markets become more efficient
Weekend news can override the statistical pattern — macro events dominate on Mondays
prior_art: Monday effect / weekend effect — French (1980), extensive academic literature
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
